one_liner: Drop-in Express 5 replacement on uWebSockets.js; hello-world suite run: ~5x Express, 1.25x actix-web req/s.
what_it_does: Fulmine.js is an Express 5-compatible web framework for Node.js 22/24/26 that replaces node:http with the uWebSockets.js native C++ addon; migration is changing require("express") to require("fulmine.js"), and a CLI (verify, migrate, profile, explain) automates the switch. It is derived from ultimate-express (the Express 4 equivalent), runs every test against real Express and compares output byte for byte, and the docs say Express 5's own suite passes (1130 passing). It is not a replacement for actix-web: that comparison only places a Node framework on a cross-language leaderboard. Extras beyond Express include cluster: 'auto', native WebSockets via app.ws(), built-in compression, pre-compressed static files and TLS via uwsOptions.
how_it_is_fast: uWebSockets.js does HTTP parsing, socket I/O and route matching in C++: routes with plain or whole-segment-parameter paths are registered on the uWS native router, and the middleware chain in front of each route is resolved once at listen(), replacing Express's per-request linear scan of the layer stack. Per-request work is lazy: the body is not read unless a handler asks, headers are not copied out of uWS unless something reads them, and no Readable/Writable stream is built unless used. A handler that only calls res.status/set/type/send/json/end with literal arguments is parsed at registration (acorn over the function source) and compiled into a uWS DeclarativeResponse that C++ answers without entering JavaScript; the opt-in 'declarative request values' setting extends this to echoing a route parameter or query value. cluster: 'auto' forks one worker per usable core (cgroup CPU quota read first), each binding the port with SO_REUSEPORT, so no primary process relays connections the way Node's built-in cluster does.
when_to_use: An existing Express 5 app where routing and dispatch, not the database or JSON.parse, is the bottleneck; the project's own CI (Node 26, self-reported) shows 1.2x-4.5x over Express on plain routing and 1.7x-5x on requests with a body.

Large route tables whose paths are plain strings or whole-segment parameters (/users/:id): the docs report 7x-22x over Express at 1,000 routes, because uWS matches in C++ while Express scans every layer.
Static or id-echo endpoints (health checks, fixed JSON) with no middleware in front and etag off, which compile to responses uWS answers with zero JavaScript per request.
Multi-core Linux hosts or containers where you want one Node process per core on one port without a primary relaying connections (cluster: 'auto', cgroup-aware).
Express apps that also need WebSockets served by the same native server (app.ws(), or socket.io via io.attachApp(app.uwsApp)).
when_not_to_use: As an alternative to actix-web: the 1.25x lead comes from a 3-route hello-world with fulmine-specific settings (etag off, connection headers off, declarative request values on), and actix-web still has the lower p99 latency at 64 and 256 connections in that run (0.39 vs 0.60 ms, 1.58 vs 2.38 ms).

Alpine/musl images, Debian bookworm images (node:26 and node:26-slim ship glibc 2.36; 2.38+ is required), Bun, Node 23/25, or builds that block git dependencies: uWebSockets.js is not on npm and is fetched from GitHub with git, and pnpm 10.26+ refuses it without an override.
Requests dominated by JSON.parse on large bodies, zlib, OpenSSL or large streams: the project's own docs cap the ratio versus Express at 1.0x-1.5x there.

Clients that upload slower than 16 KB/s (uWS drops them, not tunable from JavaScript), headers above 4 KB without UWS_HTTP_MAX_HEADERS_SIZE, or code that needs real 1xx responses (Early Hints, 100-continue), trailers or HTTP/3 (writeEarlyHints/addTrailers are no-ops; http3 is guarded off because the pinned uWS H3App segfaults on Linux).

Risk-averse production: one maintainer, first npm release 2026-08-03 with 58 versions in about seven weeks, 18 GitHub stars and ~3.4k npm downloads per month; minor releases may contain breaking changes, and CVE-2026-12590 (a body-parser limit that could be silently disabled) was fixed only in 5.21.3.

integration.dependencies: uWebSockets.js v20.71.0 (native prebuilt binaries, installed from GitHub via git), acorn, fast-zlib, tseep, iconv-lite and Express's helper modules (accepts, qs, cookie, mime-types, proxy-addr, range-parser, type-is and others); optional peer @nestjs/platform-express >=10
integration.min_toolchain: Node.js 22, 24 or 26 only (23 and 25 have no uWS binary); glibc 2.38+ on Linux; git available at npm install time
integration.platforms: Linux (glibc 2.38+, not Alpine/musl), macOS, Windows; x64 and arm64; not Bun
integration.thread_safety: Standard Node single-threaded event loop per process; cluster: 'auto' workers are separate processes that share no memory, so in-memory caches, rate-limit counters and session stores are per worker (documented); an internal worker thread reads files (threads option, default 1).

gotchas: The fast paths drop out silently: a route goes back to JavaScript routing if its path uses :from-:to, a *splat or {} groups, if a later route in the same router overlaps it, or if the request uses a different letter case; a compiled response also needs no middleware in front, literal arguments only, and etag off. Check with npx fulmine.js profile and pin it in CI with express.testing.expectNative / expectDeclarative.

'declarative request values' (used by the benchmark app) writes route parameters undecoded, so a malformed percent-encoding gets no 400 and a repeated query key gives its first value, not an array; compiled routes also answer Connection: keep-alive to a client that sent Connection: close, and param echoes go out chunked.

Requests with untrustworthy framing (duplicate Content-Length, a Transfer-Encoding not ending in chunked, unknown or lowercase methods) are refused by closing the connection with no 400, as a request-smuggling guard over uWS's permissive parser.

http.createServer(app) works but runs through node:http at Express speed; app.listen() returns the app (which passes instanceof http.Server) but no 'connection'/'request'/'upgrade' events fire, and idle timeouts are set through uwsOptions.idleTimeout.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick fulmine.js only when the code is already Node/Express and a rewrite is off the table; in the same 2026-09-24 run the compiled-language siblings are in the same range at c=512 (may_minihttp 194,372, ohkami nio 181,797, httpbeast 175,501, http.zig 171,398 req/s vs fulmine 203,996), and may_minihttp matches it at c=64 (223,705 vs 223,508) with about half the p99 latency (0.32 vs 0.60 ms). For a new service in Rust, Nim or Zig, those siblings give comparable throughput without Node, the native-addon install constraints, or a seven-week-old codebase.
verified_claims_summary: In the-benchmarker/web-frameworks develop-branch run of 2026-09-24 (commit f673364), with the server pinned to 4 cores of an undisclosed 16-thread x86_64 Linux host and zrk driving a closed loop over keep-alive connections, fulmine.js 5.21 (Node 26, uWS 20.71.0, cluster: 'auto', etag off, declarative request values on) averaged 223,508 / 210,337 / 203,996 req/s over three hello-world routes at 64 / 256 / 512 connections vs actix-web 4.8 (Rust 1.98, lto=true, codegen-units=1) at 179,203 / 168,270 / 163,415, i.e. 1.25x. In the same run Express 5.2 reached 42,586 req/s at c=512 (fulmine 4.8x), and the plain uWebSockets.js entry, started with the suite's language-level 'node cluster.mjs' command instead of fulmine's own cluster: 'auto', reached 174,621 req/s; the older master snapshot (commit 0fccb1d, older method) puts fulmine only 1.04x-1.09x ahead of actix.
status_note: Actively developed (5.21.5 released 2026-09-23, 58 npm versions since 2026-08-03) but single-maintainer and very young; Apache-2.0 and installable from npm, with the major version tracking Express rather than semver, so pin the minor.
